task: Write a cold LinkedIn message to a hiring manager that gets a reply
description: Given a job description and a brief about the applicant, generate a short, personalised cold outreach message that a hiring manager would actually respond to. The message must feel human, specific, and respectful of the reader's time.

dimensions.name: personalisation
dimensions.description: Does the message reference something specific about this company, team, or role — not generic praise? A message that could be copy-pasted to any company scores 1–3. One that references the company's specific product, recent news, or mission scores 8–10.

scoring_guide.1-3: Generic opener. 'I love your company' or 'I'm excited about this opportunity' with no specifics.
scoring_guide.4-6: Mentions the company name or role title but no deeper specificity.
scoring_guide.7-8: References something real about the company — product, mission, recent milestone.
scoring_guide.9-10: Hyper-specific: cites a particular feature, article, funding round, or team achievement that shows genuine research.

dimensions.name: relevance
dimensions.description: Does it connect the applicant's background to this specific role using a concrete example, metric, or outcome? Vague claims like 'I have relevant experience' score 1–3.

scoring_guide.1-3: No concrete connection. Just states they're interested or passionate.
scoring_guide.4-6: Mentions years of experience or job title but no specific proof.
scoring_guide.7-8: Connects a specific past project or outcome to the role's needs.
scoring_guide.9-10: Uses a concrete stat or achievement that directly mirrors what the role requires.

dimensions.name: brevity
dimensions.description: Is the message under 5 sentences? Does every sentence earn its place? Filler phrases like 'I hope this message finds you well' or 'I would love to learn more about this exciting opportunity' score 1–3.

scoring_guide.1-3: Over 6 sentences. Contains filler. Reads like a cover letter crammed into a message.
scoring_guide.9-10: 3–4 sentences. Every word is necessary. Easy to read in 10 seconds.

dimensions.name: clear_ask
dimensions.description: Does it end with ONE specific, low-friction ask? 'Would you be open to a 15-minute call this week?' scores 9–10. 'Would love to connect and discuss further' scores 1–3.

scoring_guide.1-3: No ask, or a vague 'let me know if you're interested' that puts all effort on the reader.
scoring_guide.4-6: Has an ask but it's high-friction (e.g. 'schedule a full interview') or too vague.
scoring_guide.7-8: Clear ask with a specific format (call, chat) but missing time specificity.
scoring_guide.9-10: Single, specific, low-friction ask with a time frame. Easy to say yes to.
